key_insight: LLM agents can automate both reproduction and robustness checks for scientific papers, reducing the manual burden of validating published findings.
engineering_relevance: For scientific software and AI systems, this shows how agentic workflows can be used to audit analyses, rerun experiments, and surface potentially fragile conclusions at scale.
method: Built SEER-Repro, a benchmark of 20 published SEER-based papers with reproduction resources.
Developed an AI agent to reproduce atomic claims and provide executable baselines.
Created an agentic robustness pipeline that identifies analytical choices, tests alternatives, and reruns analyses to check whether conclusions change.
evidence_signal: The agent reproduced 77.4% of 2,190 atomic claims, and the robustness pipeline flagged potentially consequential analytical choices in 9.5% of fully reproduced findings.
watch_item: Results come from a specific medical domain and benchmark, so broader generalization and expert verification remain necessary before deployment in other fields.
paper_title: AI-Driven Reproducibility and Analytical Robustness in Scientific Discovery
